docs.title: OIa Electric rights issue: Last day to buy EV scooter maker’s shares to be eligible for Rs 1,000 crore rights issue
docs.text:
Ola Electric Mobility has fixed October 13 as the record date for its Rs 1,000 crore rights issue , making today the last day for interested investors to buy shares of the EV scooter-maker to be eligible for the corporate action.
 The Bhavish Aggarwal-led company last week fixed the issue price for its rights issue at Rs 27 per equity share , around 23% lower than the stock’s previous closing price of Rs 35.13 apiece on NSE , with the amount payable in two calls.
Only those shareholders who hold Ola Electric shares in their demat accounts as of Tuesday will be eligible for the rights issue. Due to SEBI's T+1 settlement norm, investors must purchase the company's shares at least one trading day before the record date so they are credited to their demat accounts by that date and qualify for the corporate action. This effectively makes today the final day for investors to buy the shares to be eligible.
Also read | FII selloff intensifies! Foreign investors sell Indian equities worth Rs 45,000 crore in just 6 sessions. What can reverse the trend? 
 Key things to know about Ola Electric's rights issue 
Ola Electric has set the entitlement ratio at 2 rights equity shares for every 25 fully paid-up equity shares held as of the record date. The company said the issue gives all existing shareholders an opportunity to add to their holding at a substantial discount. 60% of the issue price is payable on application, with the balance due on a final call on a date to be set by the board. A two-call structure gives shareholders more time to pay.
 Live Events
Ola Electric’s rights issue will open on October 22, and close on October 30. The last date for on-market renunciation of rights entitlements is October 26. The allotments will be finalised on November 2.
Rights issue is one of the methods used by a listed company to raise additional capital. It is an invitation to existing shareholders to buy additional new shares of the company. This type of issue gives existing shareholders securities called rights. With the rights, the shareholder can buy new shares at a discount to the market price on a stated future date.
Also read | Ola Electric board approves rights; shareholders to pay in two calls 
 Ola Electric share price 
Ola Electric shares have dropped more than 5% in a week and around 6% in a month. The stock has overall fallen more than 6% in 2026 so far.
Overall, the shares of the company have fallen more than 30% in one year. The company’s current market capitalisation currently stands at around Rs 16,260 crore.

docs.title: Telecom stocks in Australia, NZ slide after SpaceX spectrum deal
docs.text:
Synopsis
 Following SpaceX's acquisition of spectrum, Telstra, TPG Telecom, and Spark New Zealand faced substantial stock drops, raising investor alarms over competitive pressure from satellite mobile services. Analysts point to Telstra's dependency on its coverage strengths amidst shifting regional pricing dynamics, although immediate subscriber impacts appear minimal. Future implications for Australia’s mobile landscape will demand careful observation as these changes unfold.
 Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen 
 Telecom stocks in Australia and New Zealand tumbled on Monday after SpaceX's acquisition of a nationwide spectrum portfolio in the US stoked fears that satellites could challenge legacy telecom firms and their network coverage.
Australia's top telecom firm Telstra shed 2.5% to finish at a six-week low, while no.3 operator, TPG Telecom , lost nearly 5% in its worst day since early June. Spark New Zealand slipped 1.8%.
Here are some details: 
SpaceX last week struck a deal to buy a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio, moving Elon Musk's satellite venture closer to mounting a direct, orbital challenge to legacy wireless giants across the United States.
That sent telecom stocks in the U.S. and Europe tumbling on concerns over growing competition from satellite-based mobile services.
Low-band spectrum can travel longer distances and penetrate buildings and other obstacles more effectively than higher-frequency airwaves.
"Investors fear the U.S. is just the first market, and that incumbents' biggest advantage, coverage, is losing its value," said David Tuckwell, CIO at ETF Shares in Sydney.
Tuckwell sees coverage-reliant Telstra as most exposed, though the near-term threat is to regional pricing power, not subscribers.
Citi analysts said, "While SpaceX's spectrum purchase is likely to weigh on Telstra's share price, it also shows the importance of having terrestrial spectrum".
Citi reiterated their "buy" call on Telstra citing upside to 2027 financial earnings guidance.
Australia's mobile market is dominated by Telstra, Singapore Telecommunications-owned Optus, and TPG Telecom, with Superloop and Aussie Broadband jostling at the fringes.
Superloop shed 2.4%, while Aussie Broadband lost nearly 2%.

docs.title: India 10-year bond yield tops 7.35% as RBI's liquidity clamp down hurts
docs.text:
(Updates at market open)
By Dharamraj Dhutia
MUMBAI, - Indian government bonds fell sharply on Monday as the central bank's measures to directly drain banking system liquidity, alongside foreign exchange operations that could indirectly reduce the surplus, weighed on demand.
The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield rose to 7.3707%, highest in three years, by 10:20 a.m. IST from 7.2994% on Friday. The yield has risen for eight consecutive weeks, gaining 54 basis points during the period.
 The Reserve Bank of India will sell 250 billion rupees ($2.58 billion) of bonds on Tuesday and require banks to maintain 99% of their daily cash reserve requirement from October 16, up from 90%.
 Advt 
The moves come days after the RBI raised its key policy rate for the first time in nearly four years and signalled more rate hikes.
At its policy meeting, the central bank announced no measures to drain liquidity, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra saying the surge in surplus cash would be temporary.
 "Such flip-flops impact the credibility and often lead to a larger reaction in asset prices, as compared to what would have been," trader with a primary dealership said.
On the currency front, the RBI sought to temper pressure on the rupee by allowing oil marketing companies to buy dollars directly from the central bank through a special window, and tightened hedging rules.
The currency measures would also lead to depletion in the rupee liquidity from the system, traders added.
Meanwhile, the benchmark Brent crude price stayed above $100 per barrel, which could impact oil-import-dependent India's inflation trajectory and government finances.
India's September retail inflation print is due later in the day, with a Reuters poll showing the print to rise 5.4% year-on-year.
 RATES
India's overnight indexed swap rates notched sharp upmoves, led by the shorter end of the curve, that is reacting more to the liquidity tightening.
The one-year OIS rate was at 6.34%, the two-year rate was at 6.53%, while the liquid five-year rate was at 6.76%.
 Advt 
($1 = 96.7600 Indian rupees)
(Reporting by Dharamraj Dhutia; Editing by Sherry Jacob-Phillips and Nivedita Bhattacharjee)

docs.title: ET Wealth Edition 18 October 2026
docs.text:
Would you order an Rs.80,000 fridge online? Dean D’Monte of Pune did. Four Diwalis ago, he bought a 564-litre side-by-side model on Amazon, swapped in his old fridge and paid about Rs 45,000. He did not fuss over the brand. The price decided it for him.
 More Indians are now making the same call. In the first half of 2026, online sales of electronics other than mobile phones grew about 22% from a year ago, and large and small appliances such as ACs, fridges, washing machines and TVs grew 25%, accord ing to a report by Redseer Strategy Consultants. A year earlier, the category had shrunk 5%.
The timing is right for the next wave. Amazon’s Great Indian Festival opened on 8 October, and Flipkart’s Big Billion Days began with early access the same day, with everyone getting in from 9 October. Banks are adding 10% instant discounts on eligible card purchases. Here is what is pulling buyers online, where stores still hold their ground, and how to make the most of the offers. 
 Momentum for online retail
Physical retail remains the larger channel for Indian consumers, but recent data from leading research and consultancy firms attest to online retail’s rapid growth.
The Kagan 2026 Asia-Pacific Consumer Insights survey by S&P Global Market Intelligence, conducted in June 2026 among 1,000 internet adults each in China, South Korea and India, shows that most Indian respondents still primarily make retail purchases from stores.
 Live Events
 ALSO READ | A paid Rs 1,64,900 upfront for iPhone 18 Pro, B chose credit card EMI, C picked no-cost EMI in festive sales – Who saved most after discounts? 
However, 41% of these Indians said they made fewer purchases at brick-and-mortar stores than a year ago, while 49% said they made more online purchases than in 2025.
According to a September report by market research firm IMARC, India’s online retail market is expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.81% between 2026 and 2034. In 2025, e-commerce marketplaces accounted for 81.3% of the market, driven by network effects, competitive pricing and broad product assortments.
The Redseer report published in September on how India’s online retail space fared in the first half of 2026 says the market grew about 25% year on year to roughly $38 billion—about Rs 3 lakh crore. This is the strongest first-half growth since H1 2022, when the nation was still in the throes of social restrictions brought on by the Covid-19 pandemic.
 Large appliances move into online basket 
During this time, D’Monte tried his luck with a large appliance bought online: a 564-litre fridge sold under Amazon’s in house Amazon Basics label.
“The side-by-side-door fridge was purchased during Diwali almost four years ago. It was the largest size available and came with a very good exchange offer. I think the price was something like Rs 80,000, which was lower than other brands such as Haier and Samsung. With the exchange of my old fridge, I got it for about Rs 45,000, nearly a 50% discount,” reveals D’Monte, 61, who worked as an assistant general manager in the human resources–facilities and administration departments of major companies over the past three decades before retiring.
Brand was not a major consideration for D’Monte while making this purchase. “When I was browsing with my nephew, he said all fridges basically come with the same functions and specifications. It is just the label that comes later,” he quips.
D’Monte’s positive experience nudged him to Amazon Basics again the following year, this time for a fully automatic, top-load, 7-kg washing ma chine. “This was bought outside the festive season. I wanted to exchange my old machine too, but it was rejected during inspection because of rusting, so I had to pay the full price, probably Rs 13,000. Still, it worked out to be cheap er than other brands,” he adds.
Since he lives by himself, D’Monte appreciates the convenience of buy ing large appliances—products that are not purchased often—from home. Though not a big spender, he says, “If something I need appears at that time, then yes, I look forward to offers dur ing the festive season.”

Among the categories it tracked, electronics—excluding mobile phones—grew about 22% year on year in H1 2026, after declining 5% in the previous year’s first half. Within this category, large and small appliances in particular--air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, TVs and dishwashers, among others—recorded 25% year-on-year growth.
Several factors lifted electronics sales in H1 2026: the rollout of the Goods and Services Tax 2.0 regime last September, which cut rates on ACs, dishwashers, monitors and large TVs from 28% to 18% (refrigerators and washing machines were already taxed at 18%); an early and longer summer that boosted demand for ACs; the 2026 Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) star-rating changeover, which pulled some purchases forward; stronger growth in Tier 2 and smaller cities; and increased participation from Gen Z buyers.

docs.title: IMF says AI investment keeps global growth around 3%, with major Asia benefits
docs.text:
Strong investment in AI infrastructure is keeping global growth at around 3%, yielding major benefits for many Asian economies that supply the hardware, such as Thailand, said Kristalina Georgieva , managing director of the International Monetary Fund.
The artificial intelligence investment boom was a "demand shock, an investment shock " that could boost growth in advanced regional economies by a half to one full percentage point, and emerging Asian economies by 0.2 to 0.8 percentage point, she said.
"So that shift into higher gear is what is keeping the world economy growing at around 3%, despite the fact we are being dragged down by the energy supply shock ," Georgieva told IMF and World Bank annual meetings in the Thai capital.

docs.title: Carlsberg India told to close Alwar unit over pollution breach ahead of $700 million IPO plans
docs.text:
Mumbai: Rajasthan's pollution control board has revoked Carlsberg India 's operating consent for its Alwar brewery and ordered its closure, citing particulate emissions nearly eight times above the permitted limit, according to a regulatory order, adding a hurdle as the Danish brewer prepares to list its Indian business through a $700 million initial public offering .
 Supplies to Rajasthan will be affected, but the impact is likely to be limited as the closure comes after the peak summer season, a senior industry official said.
The brewery also transmitted only 35.12% of its required pollution-monitoring data to the central regulator, below the mandatory threshold of 85%, the order reviewed by ET said. The state board revoked the consent to operate granted to Carlsberg India's Alwar facility on April 24, 2024, which was valid until October 31, 2028, subject to compliance with prescribed conditions. It directed the company to shut the plant and warned that failure to comply could trigger further action under air and water pollution laws. 
The order followed the central pollution regulator's inspection in July and its subsequent recommendation for closure in August. The state board also directed the local electricity distribution utility to disconnect power to the facility as part of the enforcement action.
Carlsberg India did not respond to a request for comment.
 Live Events
 You Might Also Like: 
 Carlsberg India unit, 3 other firms get Sebi nod to proceed with IPO plans
The action comes as Carlsberg India advances preparations for a stock market listing. Earlier this month, the Securities and Exchange Board of India issued its observations on the company's proposed IPO, a key regulatory step towards the offering, which is expected to raise about $700 million. Carlsberg has been preparing for a listing for about a year and could seek a valuation of around ₹30,000 crore, people aware of the matter have said. The company has not publicly confirmed a final valuation or timetable.
In February, Carlsberg chief executive officer Jacob Aarup-Andersen confirmed that the company was exploring an IPO of its Indian business, saying it was assessing whether a listing would create sufficient shareholder value.
Carlsberg India, which sells Carlsberg and Tuborg beers, reported net sales of ₹8,939 crore and net profit of ₹443 crore in the financial year ended March 2025.
Rival United Breweries , which controls about half of India's beer market, reported revenue of ₹19,400 crore and net profit of ₹442 crore in the same period. Its market capitalisation stood at ₹35,377 crore.
 You Might Also Like: 
 Glass, PET keep spirits high amid can shortage
India is an important growth market for global brewers, supported by rising incomes and a large consumer base. United Breweries leads the market, followed by Anheuser-Busch InBev and Carlsberg.
Regulatory hurdles have previously disrupted beer companies' operations in India. B9 Beverages , the maker of Bira beer , faced months of sales disruption after changing its corporate name to a public limited entity nearly two years ago. The change required labels to be re-registered and approvals to be renewed across states, leading to a write-off.

 Delhi Airport and SpiceJet issued passenger advisories on Monday as heavy rain and thunderstorms swept the national capital, warning travellers of possible flight disruptions.
 While Delhi Airport said flight operations were normal despite forecasts of inclement weather, SpiceJet cautioned that departures, arrivals and subsequent flights could be affected.
In its advisory, Delhi Airport said the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had forecast adverse weather conditions in the vicinity of the airport. 
— flyspicejet (@flyspicejet) 
The airport advised travellers to contact their respective airlines for the latest flight information.
SpiceJet, meanwhile, warned that heavy rain in Delhi could affect all departures and arrivals, as well as subsequent flights. The airline urged passengers to check their flight status on its website before travelling.
 Live Events
The advisories came as heavy rain and thunderstorms brought cooler conditions to the national capital but also triggered waterlogging in parts of the city.
The IMD forecast moderate to heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms over Delhi-NCR during the next two to three hours on Monday morning.
 Delhi weather forecast: Temperatures to remain moderate
Maximum temperatures are expected to remain between 31 and 35 degrees Celsius over the coming days, while minimum temperatures are likely to range between 22 and 25 degrees Celsius.
According to the IMD's seven-day forecast issued on Sunday evening, maximum temperatures are expected to range between 32 and 34 degrees Celsius on October 13, before rising to 33-35 degrees Celsius on October 14.
The maximum temperature is forecast to remain between 31 and 33 degrees Celsius on October 15 and 32-34 degrees Celsius on October 16 and 17.
— DelhiAirport (@DelhiAirport) 
Minimum temperatures are likely to remain between 23 and 25 degrees Celsius on October 13-15, before easing to 22-24 degrees Celsius on October 16 and 17.
 Delhi rain triggers waterlogging, traffic warnings
The morning downpour caused waterlogging in parts of the city, with the IMD warning of possible traffic disruptions, a higher risk of road accidents and water accumulation in low-lying areas and on roads.
The weather department said maximum temperatures across Delhi had fallen by 1-2 degrees Celsius over the preceding 24 hours, while minimum temperatures showed no significant change. Minimum temperatures ranged between 21 and 24 degrees Celsius, while maximum temperatures stood at 30-32 degrees Celsius.

docs.title: Sunil Bharti Mittal to receive France’s highest civilian honour from President Macron
docs.text:
Bharti Enterprises ' founder and chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal has been named a Knight of France’s National Order of the Legion of Honour , the country’s highest civilian distinction, by French President Emmanuel Macron .
 The honour recognises Mittal’s contributions to strengthening economic ties between India and France, as well as his achievements in telecommunications and digital infrastructure , Bharti Enterprises said in a statement on Monday.
The award 
Mittal said he was “moved and humbled” by the recognition and pledged to deepen economic ties between the two countries.
His association with France began in 1992, when French company Compagnie Générale des Eaux partnered with Bharti to introduce mobile telephony in India.
 Live Events
The relationship continues through his role as co-chairman of Eutelsat , the Paris-headquartered satellite communications company.
French Ambassador Thierry Mathou said in the statement that Mittal had nurtured bilateral business ties for more than three decades and highlighted his role in advancing cooperation in space and digital technology.
The Legion of Honour was established by Napoleon Bonaparte in 1802 and recognises exceptional service and achievement across business, public life, culture and science.
Mittal has earlier received the Padma Bhushan, one of India’s highest civilian awards, in 2007.
In 2024, he became the first Indian citizen to receive an honorary Knight Commander of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire (KBE) from King Charles III.
Bharti’s links with France also extend to its investment in Eutelsat.
Bharti Space participated in the satellite company’s capital raise in November 2025 and remains its largest private shareholder, with a 17.88% stake, according to the statement. The French state became Eutelsat’s largest shareholder, with a 29.65% holding.
The recognition comes as India and France continue to deepen cooperation in strategic sectors, including telecommunications, digital infrastructure and satellite communications.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

Reliance Power 's board of directors on Monday approved the issuance of up to 46.20 crore equity shares/warrants worth Rs 1,525 crore via preferential allotment mode.

The issue price of equity shares/warrants is at a discount of 13% over Monday's closing price of Rs 38.15 on the NSE. The announcement was made after market hours and Reliance Power shares on Monday ended with gains of Rs 1.81 or 4.98% over the previous closing price.
 Reliance Infrastructure Limited, the promoter of the company, will enhance its equity stake by over Rs 600 crore, a company filing said. The other investors in the preferential issue are Authum Investment and Infrastructure Limited and Sanatan Financial Advisory Services Private Limited.
The proceeds from the preferential issue will be utilised to expand business operations directly and/or through investment in subsidiaries and joint ventures, debt reduction and for general corporate purposes, the filing said.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.
 WATCH LIVE TODAY: Press conference with #FOMC Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. ET: https://t.co/1uJrua5qsH https://t.co/FJa6TbkDMt pic.twitter.com/87g5NJITsz 
— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

docs.text: Motilal Oswals research report on Canara HSBC Life InsuranceIn 2QFY27, Canara HSBC’s APE grew 11% YoY to INR6.6b (in line). For 1HFY27, APE grew 14% YoY. VNB at INR1.4b (in line) rose 20% YoY, resulting in VNB margin of 21.4% (19.7% in 2QFY26) vs. our est. of 21%. For 1HFY27, VNB grew 24% YoY with VNB margin of 21.3%. PAT grew 5% YoY to INR431m. EV at the end of 1HFY27 was INR76.2b, with an operating RoEV of 19.8%. Distribution paper is seen as net positive since CANHLIFE’s current EoM gap is comfortable vs. proposed 15%, commissions are moderate, and renewal payouts may rise. Improved affordability could further accelerate volumes, with industry-leading growth momentum to continue, as per management. While regulations are yet to be finalized, CANHLIFE’s current operations seem to be in line with the regulator’s directions in the consultation paper. We believe the key monitorable items are the impact on credit life due to regulations, GST drag, sub-debt-led improvement in solvency, and sustainability of the traditional mix. We have largely maintained our estimates considering the in-line performance in 2QFY27.OutlookWe reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR180 (based on 1.7x FY28E EV).For all recommendations report, click hereDisclaimer: The views and investment tips expressed by investment experts/broking houses/rating agencies on moneycontrol.com are their own, and not that of the website or its management. docs.title: Buy Poonawalla Fincorp; target of Rs 570: Motilal Oswal
docs.text: Motilal Oswals research report on Poonawalla FincorpPoonawalla Fincorp’s (PFL) 2QFY27 PAT stood at ~INR3.7b (in line). NII grew ~81% YoY to ~INR13.8b (in line). Other income rose ~49% YoY to ~INR2.1b. Opex rose 37% YoY to ~INR7.1b (in line), with C/I ratio broadly stable QoQ at ~45% (PY: 57%). Opex to AUM rose ~10bp QoQ to 4.15% due to ongoing investment in branches, collections, and tech Infrastructure. Management indicated that the minor sequential increase remains within the guided range, while operating leverage is expected to improve structurally over the next two years. PPoP grew ~127% YoY to ~INR8.8b (in line). Provisions stood at INR3.8b (in line), translating into annualized credit costs of ~2.15% (PQ: 2.35% and PY: ~2.75%). Management shared that 90+ dpd at 6 and 12 MOB for recent originations is ~53% better, indicating stronger early vintage credit performance and sustained improvement in portfolio quality.OutlookWe raise our FY27/FY28 EPS estimates by ~3% each to factor in slightly higher NIM (driven by stronger expansion in yields). The stock currently trades at 2.3x FY28E P/BV. We model ~44% AUM CAGR and ~120% PAT CAGR over FY26-FY28E and expect PFL to deliver RoA/RoE of 2.4%/~17% in FY28E. Axis Direct is bullish on Dr Lal PathLabs, Vijaya Diagnostic Centre and Nephrocare Health Services, assigning 'Buy' ratings to all three stocks and setting target prices that imply an upside of up to 21%, citing structural growth drivers in India's healthcare and diagnostics sector.
The brokerage has set a target price of Rs 2,315 for Dr Lal PathLabs , implying an upside of 20% from the current market price of Rs 1,934. It highlighted the company's pan-India pathology network, retail B2C business contributing over 70% of revenue, zero-net-debt balance sheet and EBITDA margins of around 26%-27%.
For Vijaya Diagnostic Centre , Axis Direct has set a target price of Rs 1,730, implying an upside of 20% from the current market price of Rs 1,437. The company operates more than 140 centres across South India, combining pathology and advanced radiology services, including MRI, CT and PET-CT imaging. The brokerage highlighted its customer stickiness and EBITDA margins of around 39%-40%.
Axis Direct has set a target price of Rs 750 for Nephrocare Health Services, also known as NephroPlus, implying an upside of 21% from the current market price of Rs 616. India's and Asia's largest specialised dialysis service provider operates 490 clinics across 269 cities in India, the Philippines, Uzbekistan and Nepal. Its network includes 255 captive hospital clinics, 176 public-private partnership (PPP) clinics and 59 standalone facilities.
Nephrocare's revenue from operations grew at a 31.5% CAGR to Rs 756 crore in FY25, while its EBITDA margin stood at 22.1%.
Axis Direct estimates India's diagnostic services market, valued at Rs 86,000-87,000 crore in FY24, will grow at a CAGR of 10%-12% to Rs 1,27,500-1,37,500 crore by FY28. The specialised renal care and dialysis segment is projected to expand at a 19.3% CAGR to around $198 crore by 2029.
The brokerage identified rising chronic disease incidence, greater awareness of early detection, a shift towards accredited organised providers and expanding government healthcare schemes and private health insurance penetration as key growth drivers.
It also highlighted improving cash generation and capital efficiency across the sector. The operating cash flow-to-EBITDA ratio has reached 70%-80% or more, while return on capital employed continues to improve alongside minimal net leverage, supporting valuations for organised healthcare and diagnostic companies.

 Taking Stock: Bears back in action; Nifty below 22,400, Sensex slumps 548 pts as IT, FMCG drag
 Broader markets outperformed the benchmark indices, with the Nifty Midcap index ending flat, while the Nifty Smallcap index advanced 1.4%.
 Rakesh Patil 
 October 12, 2026 / 16:04 IST 
 --> 
 Market Today 
 Indian benchmarks declined due to selling in key sectors.
 Sensex fell 547 points and Nifty dropped to 22,363.
 US bond yields and FII outflows weighed on sentiment.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
After rebounding in the previous session, Indian equity benchmarks came under renewed selling pressure on October 12, with the Nifty slipping towards 22,300 amid losses in IT, FMCG and financial stocks.
The indices reversed early gains as elevated US bond yields, persistent foreign investor outflows and geopolitical concerns weighed on investor sentiment.
At close, the Sensex was down 547.65 points or 0.76 percent at 71,924.68, and the Nifty was down 157.10 points or 0.70 percent at 22,363.35.
Also Read - RBI's rupee boost to spur rally, trigger swings in forward premiums 
Broader markets outperformed the benchmark indices, with the Nifty Midcap index ending flat, while the Nifty Smallcap index advanced 1.4%.
Also Read - FII selling tops Rs 45,000 crore over six sessions in October, Rs 3.6 lakh crore sold-off this year 
Biggest Nifty losers were Tech Mahindra, ITC, L&T, Hindalco, HUL, while gainers included Dr Reddy's Laboratories, Bajaj Auto, Bharat Electronics, BSE Limited and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles.
On the sectoral front, Nifty Media index added 4.6%, Auto index up 0.9%, Realty index added 1% and pharma index rose 0.3%, while Nifty IT, Metal, Private Bank, PSU Bank, FMCG down 0.4-1%.
More than 150 stocks touched 52-week low, including Avenue Supermarts, HUL, NTPC, Reliance Industries, Jupiter Wagons, Bata India, Medplus Health, Ramco Cements, TVS Holdings, Dalmia Bharat, among others. Click to View More 
Also Read - RBI’s Rupee Rescue: Administrative measures may buy time, but yield gap could force rate defence 
Among individual stocks, ideaForge Technology gained 10% after signing a loan agreement with the Technology Development Board to avail a loan of Rs 151 crore, Avenue Supermarts fell more than 4% despite reporting a 7.6% year-on-year rise in standalone Q2 profit.
IRB Infrastructure added 2% after CLSA maintained its ‘Outperform’ rating on the stock. Lenskart Solutions declined 4% after 2.93 crore shares, representing 1.67% of its equity, changed hands through block deals.
Also Read - RBI tightens forex rules: What it means for your overseas travel budget 
Viviana Power Tech advanced over 3% after securing turnkey contracts worth Rs 466.73 crore, while Can Fin Homes surged 2% after reporting a 9.2% year-on-year increase in Q2 profit.
Waterways Leisure Tourism climbed 4.5% after the company turned profitable in Q2, while Suzlon Energy gained 5% after Motilal Oswal maintained its ‘Buy’ rating with a target price of Rs 65 per share.
The Indian rupee surged 95 paise to close at 95.78 per dollar on Monday, marking its strongest single-day gain since April 2, 2026, compared with Friday’s close of 96.73.
 Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities 
The index closed in the red, forming a dark cloud cover pattern. The formation suggests that the previous day's positive momentum is losing strength, raising the possibility of a resumption bearish move.
The overall sentiment looks weak and may lead to further downside, as the spike in crude oil prices continues to weigh on equities.
On the lower end, immediate support is placed at 22,300, below which the Nifty might drift towards 22,100 or even lower. On the higher end, resistance is placed at 22,420 and 22,650.
 Ajit Mishra, SVP – research, Religare Broking 
Markets came under renewed selling pressure on Monday, giving up their early gains and extending the prevailing corrective trend. After opening on a positive note, the benchmark indices witnessed a sharp reversal and gradually moved lower as the session progressed. Consequently, the Nifty slipped towards the 22,300 mark, while the Sensex fell below 72,000, with both indices eventually settling near their respective day’s lows.
On the sectoral front, the trend remained mixed, with IT, FMCG and banking among the major laggards. In contrast, realty and auto displayed relative resilience and traded in positive territory. The broader market also showed a mixed trend, with the smallcap index gaining around 1.5%, while the midcap index ended largely flat.
Global and domestic macroeconomic concerns continued to weigh on sentiment. Although the rupee strengthened following the RBI’s recent measures to curb dollar demand, Brent crude remained elevated in the $102–105 a barrel range, limiting the relief on the inflation front. Elevated global bond yields, escalating geopolitical tensions and persistent foreign fund outflows continued to act as major headwinds. Investors also remained cautious ahead of key domestic inflation data and the ongoing corporate earnings season, both of which could influence near-term market direction.

 Sankaran Naren, CIO of ICICI Prudential MF, sees contra opportunities in mid and smallcaps: "We will only buy underperformers"
 ICICI Prudential AMC's Sankaran Naren says pockets of the mid- and smallcap space now offer contrarian opportunities, but warns investors to be patient.
 October 12, 2026 / 08:11 IST 
 Story continues below Advertisement
 Remove Ad 
 Contra funds hold up better than benchmarks in market slumps.
 The strategy focuses on buying unloved, lagging stocks.
 Contrarian investing demands long-term patience.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
With Indian equities in a slump, an investing style built around buying what others are selling is drawing attention.
 Contra funds, which buy stocks and sectors that have lagged the market, have held up better than the benchmark through the sell-off. Over the past year, the category lost 6.62 percent on average, against an 11.24 percent fall in the Nifty 50 and a 6 per cent fall in the Nifty 500.
 Over three years, contra funds have delivered 10.33 percent a year on average, well ahead of the Nifty 50's 4.18 percent and the Nifty 500 TRI's 8.73 percent.
The category is also getting crowded. SBI Contra Fund is the largest at Rs 45,068 crore, followed by Invesco India Contra Fund at Rs 20,644 crore. Bandhan and Motilal Oswal have recently launched contra funds, and the ICICI Prudential Contra Fund NFO is open until October 12, 2026.
 In the month of September all four benchmark indices saw a steep decline. The Nifty 50 fell 6.06 percent and the broader Nifty 500 lost 5.88 percent. Midcaps took the hardest hit, with the Nifty Midcap 150 down 7.09 percent. Smallcaps held up best with the Nifty Smallcap 250 down by 3.12 percent, less than half the drop in the Nifty 50. From October 1, the Nifty 50 is up by just 0.44 percen
"There is a significant differentiation in valuations and investor sentiment," said Sankaran Naren, ED and CIO, ICICI Prudential AMC. "The idea is to focus on stocks that have underperformed the market over the last three to five years, occasionally over one year, and research that addressable universe to identify investment ideas."
Contra funds can invest across large, mid and small caps. Naren currently sees more opportunity lower down the market-cap ladder. "We see contra opportunities in the mid and smallcap space, as there are many sectors where the underperformance has been pronounced. But the key principle is that we will only buy underperformers," he said.
 A common misconception is that contrarian means cheap. Naren says the label shifts with the market cycle. "Contrarian investing can include value, growth or quality stocks at different points in time. Quality underperformed over the last six years and has therefore become contrarian. But in 2020, quality would not have been bought in a contrarian fund."
The strategy's biggest demand is time. A stock that has lagged for years can keep lagging before the market recognises a turnaround.
"Investors should be mindful that contrarian investing requires patience, because the market may take time to recognise a change in fundamentals or sentiment," Naren said.
Have a horizon of at least five years. Contra bets can take years to play out, and returns can trail the market in the meantime.
Use it as a satellite, not the core. A flexi-cap or index fund can anchor the portfolio, with a contra fund adding diversification.
Check for overlap. If you already own a value fund, the two portfolios may hold many of the same stocks.
In a market where sentiment has turned sharply negative, contrarian funds offer a structured way to buy what others are avoiding, but only for investors willing to wait.

 Stock market recap: Indian equities gave up early gains and ended lower on Monday as rising bond yields and persistent foreign selling outweighed Friday's relief rally. Nifty 50 fell 157.10 points, or 0.70%, to close at 22,363.35, after opening higher and touching 22,651.10, while Sensex lost 547.65 points, or 0.76%, to settle at 71,924.68, more than 950 points below its intraday high. 
 India's 10-year bond yield rose to a three-year high of about 7.37% after the RBI tightened banks' daily cash reserve rules to drain surplus liquidity. Foreign investors sold about ₹ 45,125 crore of Indian shares in October's first six sessions, nearly matching September’s total. Iran's rejection of the latest U.S. peace proposal and weak Asian markets added to the caution, although the rupee gained about 1% after the RBI's weekend steps to curb dollar demand. 
 FMCG was the weakest sector, falling 1.67% on losses in ITC, Dabur, and HUL, followed by PSU Banks and IT. Media rallied 4.60%, while Autos, Realty, and Pharma ended higher. Breadth was evenly balanced, with 1,795 stocks advancing, 1,798 stocks declining, and 113 remaining unchanged. Upcoming inflation data and quarterly earnings will be key. 
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: Aegis Logistics Limited (current price: ₹ 1,450) 
 Why it’s recommended : Expanding LPG, liquid storage, and ammonia terminal infrastructure across key ports is expected to drive higher throughput and earnings growth. Strong growth in LPG distribution volumes, supported by rising industrial LPG demand and a nationwide logistics network, provides long-term volume visibility. 
 Key metrics : P/E: 33.03, 52-week high: ₹ 1,528.70, volume: ₹ 103.35 crore 
 Technical analysis: Trendline Breakout 
 Risk factors: Earnings remain sensitive to fluctuations in LPG/chemical import volumes, port activity, and industrial demand cycles. Large ongoing capex projects expose the company to execution delays, cost overruns, and slower-than-expected utilization risks. 
 Buy: ₹ 1,436–1,457 
 Target price : ₹ 1,700 in two to three days 
 Stop loss : ₹ 1,360 
 Buy: Pearl Global Industries Limited (current price: ₹ 1,330) 
 Why it’s recommended: Diversified manufacturing footprint across India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia, and Guatemala positions the company to benefit from global sourcing shifts away from China. Capacity expansion, strong relationships with global apparel brands, and growing order volumes support sustained revenue growth. 
 Key metrics : P/E: 38.58, 52-week high: ₹ 1,357.90, volume: ₹ 28.42 crore 
 Technical analysis: Flat base pattern breakout 
 Risk factors: High exposure to export markets makes revenues vulnerable to global economic slowdowns, apparel demand weakness, and customer order volatility. Geopolitical tensions, tariff changes, and operational disruptions across multiple manufacturing geographies can impact profitability and supply chains. 
 Buy at: ₹ 1,317–1,337 
 Target price : ₹ 1,510 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 1,240 
 How the benchmark index performed on 12 October 
 Indian equities ended lower on Monday, with Nifty 50 closing at 22,363.35, down 157.10 points or 0.70%, while Sensex declined around 600 points to 71,872. Nifty reversed early gains as investors remained cautious amid persistent foreign selling, elevated global bond yields, tighter domestic liquidity and geopolitical uncertainty. Sector performance was mixed. FMCG (-1.67%), PSU Banks (-1.18%), IT (-0.79%), and Financial Services (-0.40%) was the weak performers. Media was the standout performer, gaining 4.60%, while Auto, Realty, and Pharma rose 0.90%, 0.76% and 0.45%, respectively. 
 Overall breadth was nearly balanced, with 1,795 stocks advancing, 1,798 stocks declining, and 113 remaining unchanged, suggesting that selling was concentrated in larger index constituents rather than reflecting broad-based capitulation. The rupee remained under pressure, and elevated crude prices continued to raise concerns over imported inflation and corporate margins. Investors are likely to focus next on upcoming corporate earnings, foreign institutional flows and further signals from the Reserve Bank of India on liquidity and interest rates. 
 Nifty 50’s daily chart reflects a firmly bearish structure, with price action continuing to form lower-highs and lower-lows after breaking below the rising trendline established during the earlier recovery. The index remains below its key short- and medium-term moving averages, indicating that sellers retain control. The recent decline has been accompanied by relatively elevated volumes, lending credibility to the downward move. 
 Momentum readings remain weak: the RSI is near 34, below the neutral 50 mark and in bearish territory, although its slight recovery from oversold levels suggest that selling pressure may be easing slightly. The MACD remains below the zero line, confirming negative underlying momentum. However, the MACD line has moved above the signal line, while the histogram shows signs of contraction, indicating tentative momentum stabilisation rather than a confirmed trend reversal. 
 Nifty 50 exhibits a bearish bias, although it is currently holding above 22,180. Technically, 22,200–22,000 remains a critical support area. A decisive break below this range could accelerate downside momentum and expose the index to levels around 21,700–21,600. On the upside, 22,600–22,800 is likely to act as a significant resistance after the recent breakdown.

docs.text:
The brokerage firm highlighted that NBFC credit growth has sustained the growth momentum in Aug-26 (16% YoY), driven largely by retail and services segment.
“Not withstanding the global headwinds, the credit revival has remained strong across Banks and NBFCs in FY27, with industry segment driving the growth surge for Banks. Retail segment across vehicle, housing, unsecured credit and gold continue to witness uptick in loan growth,” the firm said in a note.
The brokerage firm further highlighted that global challenges, including inflation risks and supply chain disruptions, continue to weigh on the outlook. The RBI’s 25 basis points repo rate hike and its shift to a “calibrated tightening” stance suggest that more rate hikes may follow.
“We expect a further 50 bps increase, which could raise borrowing costs for non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). We expect our NBFC coverage universe to clock ~19% AUM CAGR during FY27-FY29E along with steady profitability. Our top picks in NBFCs are BAF (BUY) among diversifed NBFCs, CIFC (ADD) among vehicle financiers and AAVAS (BUY) and CANF (BUY) among HFCs,” the firm added.
The brokerage firm has assigned an ‘Add’ rating to L&T Finance, Piramal Finance, Aditya Birla Capital and Tata Capital, with target prices of ₹ 320, ₹ 2,000, ₹ 416 and ₹ 360, respectively.
Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company has also received an ‘Add’ rating, with a target price of ₹ 1,950, while Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services and Shriram Finance have target prices of ₹ 400 and ₹ 1,200, respectively.
Among other companies, Standard Surfactants has been assigned an ‘Add’ rating with a target price of ₹ 5,000, while CreditAccess Grameen has a target price of ₹ 1,570.

docs.title: Retail stocks to buy before Q2 results: Metro Brands, Campus Activewear, Vishal Mega Mart shares — Elara recommends
docs.text:
Elara Securities has assigned a Buy rating to Vishal Mega Mart, Page Industries, Vedant Fashions, Safari Industries, Dollar Industries, Metro Brands and Campus Activewear. The brokerage has an Accumulate rating on VIP Industries, Bata India and Relaxo Footwears, while Go Fashion has been rated Reduce. In its retail sector preview, Elara Securities expects its retail coverage universe to deliver revenue growth of around 11.8% year-on-year (YoY) and EBITDA growth of approximately 12.7% in Q2FY27. Aggregate EBITDA margins are projected to improve by about 13 basis points to 15.5%, as operating leverage offsets inflation in cotton and crude-linked input costs. Premium categories are expected to continue outperforming, while demand in the mid-market segment is likely to remain selective and promotion-led. Organised retailers could also gain market share from smaller players, which continue to face pressure from elevated input costs, the brokerage said. Festive demand fell in the base quarter last year, when Navratri began on 22 September 2025. This year, the festival shifts to Q3FY27, while the Shraddh period is expected to delay some purchases until late September, according to Elara Securities. The brokerage expects apparel revenue across its coverage universe to decline by around 3.8% YoY in Q2FY27, with EBITDA falling approximately 5%, as subdued demand, input cost inflation and operating deleverage weigh on performance. Vishal Mega Mart is expected to outperform, with revenue projected to grow 17.5% YoY and same-store sales growth (SSSG) estimated at around 6%, supported by store additions. In contrast, Vedant Fashions and Go Fashion are expected to report modest SSSG of approximately 1% and 0.6%, respectively. Delayed festive demand, weak off-season wedding demand and ongoing store rationalisation are likely to constrain their performance. Footwear demand remains healthy, driven by premiumisation, calibrated price increases and expansion across retail and digital channels, Elara Securities said. The brokerage expects its footwear coverage universe to post revenue growth of around 8.8% YoY and EBITDA growth of 10% in Q2FY27. Metro Brands is expected to lead the segment, with projected revenue growth of 13.2% YoY, supported by higher volumes and a favourable product mix. Relaxo Footwear's recovery is expected to be driven by improved realisations, although margins may remain under pressure. Bata India, meanwhile, is likely to report modest revenue growth but a stronger profit after tax (PAT) recovery, aided by lower markdowns and cost-control measures. The innerwear segment is expected to record revenue growth of approximately 11% YoY in Q2FY27, supported by volume momentum at Page Industries , the spillover of three days of undelivered billing from Q1, and the impact of May's price increase. New product initiatives, including the Disney-Marvel launch and expansion in athleisure, are also expected to support demand. However, profitability may remain under pressure at Page Industries and Dollar Industries as higher-cost cotton inventory flows through the cost of goods sold. Recent price increases are expected to partly offset input cost inflation, while Dollar Industries could face additional pressure from volume weakness following price hikes and elevated employee costs. The organised luggage segment is expected to sustain its recovery, supported by new product launches, price increases and a weak base at VIP Industries. Elara Securities projects revenue growth of around 10.9% YoY for the segment. Safari Industries is expected to report growth of approximately 11%, aided by e-commerce traction. VIP Industries' EBITDA loss is likely to narrow materially, although its EBITDA margin is expected to remain negative at around 9%. Elevated discounting, higher resin costs linked to crude oil prices and increased marketing expenditure could weigh on profitability. Safari Industries' EBITDA margin is expected to contract by around 193 basis points, according to the brokerage. The key factors for retail investors in Q2FY27 will be the timing of festive purchases, demand trends across price segments, store expansion and the extent to which retailers can pass on higher input costs. While value retail, footwear, and innerwear are expected to support sector growth, apparel retailers could face near-term pressure due to the shift in festive demand into Q3FY27. Elara Securities' preference for Metro Brands, Campus Activewear and Vishal Mega Mart reflects its focus on companies with stronger growth prospects. docs.title: Frenzied stock-options trading shows individual investors are still hungry for risk
docs.text:
Global 
 Frenzied stock-options trading shows individual investors are still hungry for risk
 Krystal Hur , Hannah Erin Lang , The Wall Street Journal 4 min read 13 Oct 2026, 06:39 AM IST 
 Summary
 Trading in single-stock options contracts are near levels reached in 2021, when a new generation of amateur investors shook up Wall Street. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Individual investors aren’t letting anything get them down these days.
 Their fervor is showing up in frenzied trading of options, or contracts that allow holders to buy or sell a stock at a set price, by a certain date. Volumes in options tied to individual stocks have recently reached levels seen during the meme-stock mania of 2021, about $700 billion of notional volume a day, according to Carrick Lane, an investment manager specializing in options strategies. The prices of call options, which give the right to buy, have eclipsed levels seen during that time.
 A new generation of individual investors discovered the markets during the post-Covid rally, and by early 2021 many amateur traders were pushing into more complicated, and often riskier, bets. A boom in stock options and other derivatives was under way.
 Those markets are now abuzz with retail activity once again, and Wall Street knows the reason: Individual investors are looking past rising interest rates, $100 oil prices and war in the Middle East . They are focusing on strong corporate earnings, and as comfortable rolling the dice on volatile markets as they were back when GameStop, Roaring Kitty and AMC Entertainment were the talk of Reddit forums.
 Bullishness among individual investors, as measured by the percentage who expect stock prices to rise over the next six months, reached 40.3% for the week ended Oct. 7, according to the latest survey from the American Association of Individual Investors. That is the highest level since mid-July and comparable to levels seen in 2021.
 Many, like 41-year-old Kunal Berry, are buoyed by the success of the artificial-intelligence trade and optimistic about the technology’s potential to transform business and the economy.
 “The growth is there,” the Los Angeles-based consultant said. Berry has chased gains in megacap tech names including Nvidia, Amazon and SpaceX. “The short-term volatility—you’ve just got to have the stomach for it,” he said.
 The meme-stock craze might have faded as many of the era’s favorite stocks eventually lost their luster. But individual investors’ enthusiasm for the markets has only grown stronger over the past five years. This cohort kept “buying the dip” even during April 2025, when a global trade war rattled professional investors and triggered a deep selloff. They helped crown a new class of AI darlings and piled into the SpaceX initial public offering. And they are still buying today.
 On Monday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.4%, or about 196 points. The S&P 500 fell less than 0.1% and the Nasdaq composite lost 0.4%.
 In another sign investors are feeling much as they did in 2021, more traders are comfortable betting on short-term price moves. More than half of current single-stock options volumes are concentrated in contracts less than two weeks away from expiring, according to John Marshall, a partner at Carrick Lane.
 One reason behind their persistent optimism is strong corporate profits, which have helped drive stocks to repeated records this year. Companies in the S&P 500 are expected to report earnings growth of about 30% for the third quarter from the prior year, according to FactSet. For 2026, profits are expected to jump 33%.
 Individual investors have grown a bit more selective in 2026, analysts say, opting to throw their weight behind a few high-conviction names over buying broader market dips. And retail activity slowed during the summer, following an explosive rally in shares of memory stocks and chip makers that peaked in June. But that summer cool-down historically tends to reverse in October, according to data from Citadel Securities—and DIY traders could be even more plugged in through the rest of the year.
 Not everyone is all-in on derivatives, either. But even more risk-averse investors are staying in the market.
 The top position bought by Charles Schwab’s clients in September was an exchange-traded fund tracking the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index. That is the first time an ETF has taken that spot since Schwab began collecting that data in 2021. Clients also snapped up call options tied to ETFs last month, according to Schwab.
 “It’s a little bit more cautious optimism,” said Joe Mazzola, head trading strategist at Charles Schwab. “They’re definitely looking to buy dips.”
 Write to Krystal Hur at krystal.hur@wsj.com and Hannah Erin Lang at hannaherin.lang@wsj.com

 1. FROM MY DESK
 A deadly attack on Saudi Arabia’s main airport over the weekend exposed a deepening crisis for Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The strikes by Iran-backed Houthi militants killed at least 12 people and injured hundreds more.
 With threats mounting, the crown prince is shuttling between heavily guarded palaces equipped with bunkers. The violence threatens his ambitions to turn Saudi Arabia into a global tourism and investment hub. Summer Said and Georgi Kantchev examine how Mohammed’s own decisions have contributed to his predicament, with rising defense and infrastructure costs threatening to siphon away funds needed for the economic diversification push.
 The attacks are also wreaking havoc on global air travel. Airlines canceled more than 1,000 flights, as threats to Saudi airspace jeopardize one of the last two major air corridors connecting Europe and Asia.
 This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here. If you’re reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.

 4. READ IT HERE FIRST
 The welfare state is crushing Britain.
 A soaring number of people on sickness or disability benefits is blowing up the U.K.’s welfare bill and imperiling its financial stability. Some seven million people—more than 10% of the population—now claim at least one of the benefits, driven by a fourfold surge in psychiatric claims. With spending on track to hit £130 billion, or $172 billion, Max Colchester and David Luhnow report on how Britain faces a looming financial reckoning as leaders struggle to make politically painful cuts.
 5.
 A new type of mortgage is reviving long abandoned neighborhoods.
 Known as a debt-service coverage ratio loan, this specialized mortgage is approved based on potential rental income rather than a borrower’s wealth. The model is helping real-estate investors buy, renovate and rent out vacant and dilapidated homes. These private mortgages are injecting capital into long-disinvested communities across cities like Baltimore, Detroit and Cleveland. Nicholas G. Miller lays out how the flexible loans are fueling a neighborhood renaissance while drawing scrutiny over fraud risks.

docs.title: RIL shares: Reliance Industries stock slides 6% in a month, can Jio Platforms IPO aid the bounce back? Experts' views
docs.text:
Irrespective of this value-unlock factor, experts believe the Jio Platforms IPO is a central factor, though not entirely negative. While news of an upcoming mega public offering usually acts as a catalyst, market sentiment has cooled because recent reports put valuations at approximately $114 billion (~ ₹ 10.3 lakh crore), lower than earlier speculative estimates of $130 billion to $170 billion. They said Reliance shares are facing a hurdle at ₹ 1,200. On breaking above this, we can expect the Reliance share price to scale around ₹ 1265. Reliance share price today is around ₹ 1165, clocking around 6% dip in one month. Whether Jio Platforms IPO can bring the mojo in Reliance shares, Seema Srivastava, Senior Research Analyst at SMC Global Securities, said, “Jio Platforms IPO is structured predominantly as a fresh capital issue of around 2.9% post-IPO equity rather than a massive offer-for-sale (OFS). This means RIL itself is not directly pocketing cash from selling its stake, though it retains a controlling ~64.5% stake while Jio uses the proceeds for debt prepayment and expansion.” The SMC Global Securities expert said that arbitrage traders and institutional desks are temporarily discounting the holding company valuation until the listing price band and post-listing trading performance establish firm market values. Therefore, while the lower-than-anticipated IPO valuation guidance created temporary selling pressure alongside weakening energy metrics, the IPO itself remains a strategic structural positive for unlocking long-term value once primary market demand stabilises. On what technical chart hints at the Reliance Industries shares, Mahesh M Ojha, VP — Research and Business Development at KC Securities, said, “Immediate support for the Reliance Industries shares is placed at ₹ 1145, whereas ₹ 1120 is acting as major support for RIL shares. Those with a long-term horizon are advised to hold the scrip, maintain a stop-loss at ₹ 1085, and keep accumulating on every 4%-5% dip. Fresh investors can apply the same by adding Reliance Industries to their portfolio at the current market price.” Ojha said that Reliance Industries shares are facing resistance at ₹ 1200. docs.text:
Global 
 The mystery of the unknown sailor who inspired Trump to shake up the Navy
 Marcus Weisgerber , The Wall Street Journal 6 min read 13 Oct 2026, 06:42 AM IST 
 Summary
 A chance encounter pushed the president to revamp the carrier fleet—and sent the Pentagon on a hunt for the elusive “Bill Jones.” 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 In August, President Trump directed the Navy to figure out how to return to using steam catapults on aircraft carriers to hurl fighter jets into the air.
 For U.S. military officials, the order marked the return of an old foe: Bill Jones.
 Who?
 Exactly. Trump has described the man as a “catapulter” who served in the Navy for 25 years and loves the smell of steam. Jones convinced Trump the old technology was superior to modern methods of launching jets, the president said.
 The incident sent Navy leaders searching for Jones to figure out what he said that prompted the president to demand an overhaul of one of the most expensive weapons programs in history. They never found him, according to defense officials.
 But they’re still dealing with the consequences of the mystery sailor and his chance encounter with the president.
 It all started just months into Trump’s first term when he was in Virginia touring the USS Gerald R. Ford, the newest aircraft carrier in the Navy’s fleet.
 This warship, the largest in the world and first in its class, cost about $19 billion but had experienced myriad problems over eight years of construction as cutting-edge, but unproven, technology was installed on the ship. It was years behind schedule and billions of dollars over budget.
 Trump seemed eager to apply his real-estate experience to the dazzlingly complex world of Pentagon procurement. He has said he grew tired of hearing excuses from the admirals and he wanted to hear from the people who operate the machinery.
 “I said, ‘Let me see the catapult people,’” Trump recalled during an April 2019 speech. “They said, ‘Sir, you don’t really want to do that?’ I said, ‘Yeah, those are the people that know what the hell they’re doing.’”
 Then it happened.
 The president said a sailor told him the Navy was making a mistake by ditching the tried-and-true method of using steam catapults. The decision to use an electromagnetic system to launch planes faster and more efficiently was dooming the service to failure.
 The USS Abraham Lincoln uses a steam catapult to conduct flight operations in the Arabian Sea. (US Navy)
 Trump has said the sailor told him if the electric catapults break you need geniuses from MIT to repair them, while the steam version can be fixed with a hammer and blowtorch. Industry officials said both descriptions vastly oversimplify things.
 After the encounter, Navy officials scrambled to explain to the president why the technologies were chosen and why removing them would be extremely disruptive, according to former defense officials.
 During a Thanksgiving call in November 2018 to sailors aboard the USS Ronald Reagan, an older Nimitz-class carrier with steam catapults, Trump asked the ship’s commanding officer his opinion of steam versus electric catapults.
 Then-Capt. Patrick Hannifin, now a three-star admiral in charge of naval forces in the Western Pacific and Indian Oceans, told Trump that while steam is reliable now, he preferred electromagnetic catapults.
 When Trump pressed Hannifin that “you have to be Albert Einstein” to operate them properly, the captain responded: “You sort of have to be Albert Einstein to run the nuclear power plants that we have here as well, but we’re doing that very well.”
 Trump said “that’s actually a very good answer.” The issue seemed to go away.
 It came roaring back as Trump sought and won re-election.
 He mentioned Jones by name during a January 2024 rally in Mason City, Iowa. Then in February 2025, Trump brought up the electric catapults when he swore in Tulsi Gabbard to be the director of national intelligence.
 There were rumors among industry insiders that Trump would sign an executive order telling the Navy to return to steam, but nothing happened—until this summer.
 In August, Trump signed a national security memorandum directing the Navy to figure out the cost and timeline for installing steam catapults and hydraulic elevators in the ship currently known as CVN 81, expected to join the fleet in 2034.
 The Navy isn’t getting its Ford-class carriers fast enough, and must simplify their design by using time- and battle-tested technology, an administration official said.
 It hasn’t built a carrier with steam since the USS George H.W. Bush, which entered the fleet in 2009.
 More problematic: “Steam catapults have been out of production for decades—no one makes them anymore,” said Hunter Stires, the maritime strategist to former Navy Secretary Carlos Del Toro.
 Since the order, Navy leaders have couched their public remarks.
 “If we were to go back to steam and hydraulics with the elevators, we need to really understand the total cost of that,” Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle said at a conference in Reno, according to USNI News. “That will be a significant design change.”
 He said a February stress test of the Ford’s electromagnetic launchers showed they outperformed their steam peers.
 An aircraft taking off via electric catapult on the USS Gerald R. Ford in January 2020. (Marcus Weisgerber/WSJ)
 Analysts and industry insiders say the new system could be more effective for future warfare since it could launch bomb-laden aircraft and drones. Shipbuilding experts worry putting steam back on a carrier would put the Navy technologically behind China.
 Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao has warned officials not to question the president’s decision.
 “To be clear, the debate on whether we do this has ended,” he wrote in an Aug. 28 memo, referring to a broader set of recommendations including the steam catapults.

docs.title: Uncapped coverage: Is your health policy really ‘unlimited’?

Mint Money 
 Uncapped coverage: Is your health policy really ‘unlimited’?
 Aprajita Sharma 9 min read 12 Oct 2026, 01:05 PM IST 
 Summary
 Unlimited health plans from Niva Bupa, Care, ICICI Lombard and HDFC ERGO work in different ways, and some retain caps or conditions despite the label. What exactly is unlimited, and what conditions continue to apply when a large claim arrives? 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 How much health insurance is enough when medical costs outpace incomes? While a ₹ 10 lakh cover seems adequate today, prolonged ICU stays, complex surgeries, or treatments for rare diseases can easily exceed standard limits. 
 To address this, insurers now offer unlimited health insurance plans. Rather than capping the base sum insured (SI), these policies pay eligible hospital bills, whether they are ₹ 8 lakh or ₹ 80 lakh. However, not every unlimited health plan works this way —some use uncapped base limits, while others rely on infinite renewal bonuses or unlimited restoration features.
 Here is how four major offerings compare:
 Niva Bupa ReAssure 3.0: unlimited cover, but check the room category
 Niva Bupa ReAssure 3.0 has four variants—Classic, Select, Elite and Black. Customers can choose a ₹ 5 lakh, ₹ 10 lakh or unlimited sum insured.
 “You can buy any variant, either having ‘unlimited’ sum insured or a base cover of ₹ 5 lakh or ₹ 10 lakh. A higher sum insured is not possible. It has to be either ₹ 5 lakh, ₹ 10 lakh or unlimited,” said Ashish Kumar, founder, Sri Shani Financial Services. 
 According to data from insurance corporate agent Nyvo Insurance Services, the Black variant with ₹ 10 lakh cover and the Booster+ no-claim bonus rider costs ₹ 17,356 for a 30-year-old male from Mumbai. The unlimited option costs ₹ 23,836, about 37% more. 
 Booster+ adds 100% of the base SI for every claim-free year, up to 10 times the base SI in limited coverage options. Thus, on a ₹ 10 lakh policy, paying three annual premiums builds the cover to ₹ 30 lakh at the beginning of the third policy year ( ₹ 10 lakh base SI + ₹ 20 lakh booster+). If you then make an ₹ 18 lakh claim during the third year, ₹ 10 lakh comes from the base SI and ₹ 8 lakh from the bonus, leaving ₹ 12 lakh in the booster+ balance. At the beginning of the fourth year, cover becomes ₹ 32 lakh ( ₹ 10 lakh base SI + ₹ 12 lakh remaining booster+ + ₹ 10 lakh fresh booster+), not ₹ 40 lakh. 
 However, accumulated cover does not increase every benefit. Modern treatments and sub-limits, such as air ambulance cover, may remain linked to the base SI. 
 With unlimited SI, modern treatment is capped at ₹ 1 lakh under the Classic and Select plans. Room eligibility also varies: general ward for Classic, twin-sharing for Select, all rooms except deluxe and suite for Elite, and all room categories for Black, Kumar said. 
 “Even with unlimited SI, non-payable items like gloves, masks, PPE kits, syringes and nebulizer kits will not be covered unless the customer buys the Safeguard+ add-on,” he added. 
 This makes the choice between an unlimited variant and a high base SI with accumulated bonus less straightforward than it appears. 
 Care Ultimate Care: modest premium differential
 Care Health’s Ultimate Care builds cover through its Infinity Bonus, which adds 100% of the base sum insured annually, regardless of claims, with no upper limit. This is over and above a cumulative bonus of 50% of the base sum insured annually, capped at 100%. For example, on a ₹ 10 lakh policy, at the beginning of the second year, the total cover would be ₹ 25 lakh ( ₹ 10 lakh base SI + ₹ 10 lakh bonus + ₹ 5 lakh cumulative bonus). At the beginning of the third year, it would rise to ₹ 40 lakh ( ₹ 10 lakh base SI + ₹ 20 lakh bonus + ₹ 10 lakh cumulative bonus). From year four, only the unlimited bonus of ₹ 10 lakh a year is added, as the cumulative bonus has reached its cap. 
 The plan also provides an additional amount equivalent to the first policy year's sum insured after seven claim-free years. 
 According to Nyvo data, a 30-year-old male from Mumbai would pay ₹ 21,559 for a ₹ 20 lakh cover with the Infinity Bonus. The unlimited option costs ₹ 23,111, according to Nyvo data, about 7% more than the ₹ 20 lakh option. 
 “Before you make a choice, you must know that advanced technology methods, Ayush treatment, domiciliary treatment, among others, will be limited to the base sum insured if you choose the limited-SI option,” said CA Mayank Gosar, founder and chief executive officer, Softcon Capital. 
 “On a base SI of ₹ 20 lakh or ₹ 25 lakh, the premium differential with the unlimited option is hardly significant if you take the Infinity Bonus and Unlimited Care rider, under which one claim is covered without a limit. In that sense, going with the unlimited option makes sense,” Gosar added. 
 ICICI Lombard Elevate: unlimited or build up the cover
 ICICI Lombard's Elevate offers both an unlimited sum-insured option and features that allow customers with a defined SI to build up substantial coverage. 
 “We launched the unlimited option in July 2024 along with the launch of Elevate. The idea was to give comprehensive coverage to all, as per their needs,” said Priya Deshmukh, head of health products, operations & services at ICICI Lombard . “There are people who do not want to get into the hassles of increasing their sum insured as their life cycle changes or managing multiple policies. For them, our unlimited option is good even though it is expensive. But the difference is marginal if you compare ₹ 1 crore or ₹ 50 lakh coverage with unlimited.”
 According to Nyvo data, a 30-year-old male from Mumbai would pay ₹ 19,667 for a ₹ 20 lakh cover with the Power Booster add-on. The feature increases the annual sum insured by up to 100% every year. 
 The unlimited option costs ₹ 32,685, about 66% more than the ₹ 20 lakh cover. 
 Elevate’s Infinite Care offers un

docs.title: Nobel Prize 2026: Why Hall and Woodford’s economic research resonates in today’s world
