docs.title: Persistent Systems secures 94% stake in Nagarro, plans squeeze-out of minority shareholders
docs.text: Persistent Systems said that it has secured 94.04% of the share capital and voting rights of Nagarro SE. The figure comes after the additional acceptance period for its voluntary public takeover offer ended on October 6. The company plans to squeeze out the remaining minority shareholders once the deal closes. Persistent-Nagarro takeover crosses 90% threshold The offer was made through Galaxy Germany Holding SE, a wholly owned direct subsidiary of Persistent. It covered all outstanding shares of Nagarro. The minimum acceptance threshold was 50% plus one share. A further 1,335,114 Nagarro shares were tendered during the additional acceptance period. Another 7,568,145 shares had been tendered in the initial period. In total, 8,903,259 shares have now been tendered. That represents about 71.94% of Nagarro's share capital and voting rights. ALSO READKEC International bags transmission and distribution orders worth Rs 1,014 crore Persistent already holds about 22.10% under a share purchase agreement with Lantano Beteiligungen GmbH. Together, the two stakes add up to about 94.04%. Nagarro minority shareholders face squeeze-out Persistent said it holds more than 90% of Nagarro's share capital and voting rights. It said it plans to initiate a squeeze-out of the remaining minority shareholders upon closing. The company described this as part of a take-private strategy. No final decision has been taken, Persistent said. It will share details of the specific measures in due course. Nagarro deal closing targeted for March 2027 Persistent expects the transaction to close by the end of the first quarter of calendar year 2027. Closing is subject to a limited number of outstanding regulatory approvals. “The final results of our offer for Nagarro are a clear endorsement of the strategic logic behind bringing Persistent and Nagarro together. We now look forward to completing the remaining steps toward closing. Together, we will build the global AI-led digital engineering player we envision.” Sandeep Kalra, chief executive officer and executive director of Persistent Systems, said. ALSO READSaatvik Green Energy bags Rs 100 crore order to supply 5,000 solar pumps in Maharashtra Nagarro takeover governed by German law The offer is governed by German law, in particular the Wertpapiererwerbs- und Übernahmegesetz, or WpÜG. Certain United States securities law provisions on cross-border takeover offers also apply. In the US, the offer was made under Section 14(e) and Regulation 14E of the Exchange Act, using the Tier II exemption. The full terms are set out in the offer document authorised by Germany's financial regulator, BaFin. The company also said the Bidder may acquire additional Nagarro shares outside the offer, subject to German law. About Persistent Persistent Systems delivers AI-led, platform-driven digital engineering and enterprise modernisation to businesses across industries. The company has over 28,500 employees in 21 countries. Its services include software engineering, product development, data and analytics, CX transformation, cloud computing and agentic business automation. It is part of the MSCI India Index and key NSE indices, including the Nifty Midcap 50 and Nifty IT. Persistent has said it has achieved carbon neutrality. Persistent Systems share price today Persistent Systems’ share price increased 4.77% in the past month. Furthermore, Persistent Systems’ share price increased 7.55% in the past year.

docs.title: Democrats have a 93% chance of flipping the House: What could happen to stocks next?
docs.text: A Democratic win in the November 3 midterm elections could affect the bond market more than the equity market. This could happen if Democrats win both Houses, or at least one House with a sizeable majority. US Treasury yields are at multi-decade highs across the notes of different durations. In case of a gridlock, investors would rush to purchase safe-haven assets, pushing bond prices higher and driving US Treasury bond yields lower. This is what many market experts believe will happen in the bond market. Despite ongoing geopolitical tensions and rising oil prices fuelling inflation, how far the fall in yields holds on remains to be seen. Democrats are the favorites to flip the House As of October 11, Nate Silver's FLIPR's Deluxe model shows Democrats' chances of retaking the House at up to about 93%. Overall, polls show a Democratic lead of 9.5 points, with 51.1% support for Democrats and 41.6% for Republicans. The market base case is that Democrats take the House, and the Senate is a toss-up, or too close to call. That is the base case, not a certainty. ALSO READUS Midterms vs Stocks: What history says could happen after election day Why are investors watching this election so closely? Investors around the world are concerned about what the midterms could mean for markets. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq have shown remarkable resilience through a turbulent 2026. The S&P 500 is on pace for its fourth consecutive year of double-digit returns. With Democrats expected to control at least one chamber of Congress, investors can expect more volatility and uncertainty. Negotiations over the budget, debt ceiling, defense spending and AI regulation could all get harder. On the latest episode of "Let's talk investments" from Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank's Chief Investment Office, CIO Chris Hyzy spoke with Libby Cantrill, head of Public Policy at PIMCO, the global bond firm. "Usually, the midterm election is a referendum on the party in power," says Cantrill. The House has a slim Republican majority. The party not in power has historically gained 26 seats. That makes the House the likeliest chamber to change hands. In the Senate, Democrats need "a perfect night," she adds. That means a net gain of four seats, including wins in states that have gone Republican in recent presidential elections. Could a Democratic sweep rattle markets? A change in control, particularly a House-Senate Democrat sweep, could generate volatility, Cantrill says. "But I'm not sure that's well placed." Any election scenario is likelier to produce gridlock and the need for negotiation, rather than sweeping policy changes, she adds. Markets would likely recover quickly. "The year after the midterms is usually a good year for equities." What does history say about markets after elections? The numbers are encouraging. In the post-war period, the S&P 500 rose 100% of the time in the six and 12 months following elections, averaging 13% and 14%, respectively. Even over three months, markets ended higher 90% of the time. The last three months of the year tend to be the strongest, with October standing out, ending higher 67% of the time. On average, Q4 has gained 5.6% since 1930, far surpassing the preceding three quarters of election years. Greater clarity about the US fiscal policy path could be a tailwind for investors after the election. US debt tops $40 trillion, but action may wait What could the election mean for US debt and the bond market? With both parties eager to spend and reluctant to raise taxes, the election, regardless of outcome, probably won't prompt immediate efforts to control US debt, Cantrill believes. The debt has doubled since 2017 and recently topped $40 trillion. Lawmakers may wait until mounting pressure forces action. "I think that deficits and debt will be a focus of the presidential election come 2028," she says. When the time comes, relatively low US taxes give lawmakers "a longer runway than Japan or Europe to raise taxes if necessary." The debt is a serious long-term problem, she adds. Even so, it has yet to deter bond investors, who are attracted to yields on 10-year Treasuries that currently top 5%. Bottom line: stay focused on fundamentals "Whatever the outcome of the election, history suggests that reacting to short-term political uncertainty rarely rewards long-term investors," says Hyzy. In fact, he says, "We believe short-term election-related volatility may create potential opportunities to add strategically to a portfolio." Volatility tends to rise during midterm years. Over longer horizons, equity returns and economic strength are shaped less by election outcomes than by corporate profits, valuations, labor market conditions and capital investments. While volatility could rise as election day nears, seasonal trends turn increasingly constructive into year-end and after the election. For investors, the implication is straightforward: look through short-term political uncertainty, stay focused on fundamentals, and maintain a long-term perspective. Disclaimer: This article is for educational purposes only. It does not constitute a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Market history does not guarantee future results. Readers should consult a qualified financial advisor before making investment decisions.

docs.title: Jio changed telecom, Starlink faces the test
docs.text: Jio Platforms’ much-anticipated initial public offering will hit the market later this month, and the company has an interesting story to tell investors. It entered a crowded telecom market and upended its economics by shifting the focus from voice to data, changing the sector’s entire business model. The updated red herring prospectus is expected during the week. The IPO will put the spotlight on a company that has grown from a mobile connectivity disruptor into a wider digital ecosystem spanning cloud, artificial intelligence, and enterprise services. It may be a coincidence, but Elon Musk’s allegations that Indian business houses are blocking Starlink to protect their monopolies, with Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani among his apparent targets, have come just as Jio prepares to enter the public markets. However, the record of Indian telecom is not one of companies unwilling to compete. It is a story of businesses that have repeatedly adapted to competition and technological change, and of a market that has been transformed by new entrants and new business models. ALSO READModi@25: Steady agri-growth Jio’s entry demonstrated how a new player could alter an established market. Its low-cost data strategy changed consumption patterns and forced incumbents to respond, while the ensuing consolidation left the market with three major private mobile operators: Jio, Bharti Airtel, and Vodafone Idea. The reduction in the number of players has raised legitimate questions about market concentration, but competition has continued through tariff changes, differentiated offerings, and the battle to retain customers. Airtel, meanwhile, has expanded well beyond India, building a substantial presence across Africa. Indian telcos have competed with global players, taken their businesses overseas, and devised pricing and distribution models suited to local conditions. Their record hardly suggests that they would automatically shy away from a new technology or competitor. Their partnerships with global technology companies underline this point. Meta invested $5.7 billion in Jio Platforms in 2020, and has since partnered with Reliance on digital commerce and AI initiatives. In June, the two announced a collaboration involving an AI data centre in Jamnagar, Gujarat, with an initial capacity of 168 Mw. Google, in contrast, has partnered with both Jio and Airtel across digital services, cloud, and AI. It has worked with Jio on affordable devices and digital services, while its relationship with Airtel includes cloud and AI initiatives. Google is also partnering with AdaniConneX and Airtel on its proposed AI hub in Visakhapatnam. This is the context in which Musk’s claims need to be assessed. Starlink has signed distribution agreements with both Jio and Airtel, potentially giving it access to their retail networks, business customers, and infrastructure. Starlink gets an established route to market, while the Indian operators gain another connectivity service to offer, particularly in areas where terrestrial networks are difficult or expensive to deploy. These partnerships do not rule out commercial rivalry or disagreements. But they complicate the suggestion that Indian telcos are simply trying to shut Starlink out. A company can compete with another in one area and collaborate with it in another. That said, satellite communications pose regulatory and security challenges different from those of conventional mobile networks. Authorities need confidence that security directions can be enforced, unauthorised use addressed, and network operations kept within Indian law. Starlink, Jio Satellite Communications, and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb have licences but need to meet the remaining requirements before commercial operations can begin. So, they are at broadly the same stage of the process. ALSO READFifth column by Tavleen Singh: Congress party must do more than protest There is also a difference between opening a market and guaranteeing mass adoption. Satellite broadband can connect remote communities, businesses, and institutions beyond the reach of fibre or reliable mobile coverage. But it is not automatically a substitute for affordable terrestrial broadband. If indicative estimates of terminal costs around `8,000 and monthly subscriptions above `3,000 hold up when the pricing is announced, the service will remain beyond the reach of many households. So, early market is likely to be concentrated among enterprises, institutions, affluent users, and locations where conventional connectivity is unavailable or unreliable. That would make it a useful addition to the market, but not an immediate challenger to mass-market mobile services. Musk should also remember that a strong global brand does not guarantee success in India. Tesla has entered the Indian electric vehicle market, but its high prices and limited product range have so far kept sales modest. This should be a reminder that Indian consumers do not buy a name alone; price, suitability, and the value on offer matter. Starlink will face the same test. Securing regulatory approval is only the first step. It will have to find customers, offer a compelling proposition, and compete with terrestrial networks wherever those networks can deliver connectivity more economically. The irony is that Musk, while accusing Indian business houses of protecting monopolies, is seeking entry into a market where those same companies have built businesses by challenging incumbents and adapting to new technologies. Indian telcos have not shied away from competition, and there is little reason to assume they will start doing so now. Tesla has discovered that India is not a market where global prestige alone guarantees a win. Starlink may find the same. The government must ensure a fair and transparent route to entry, but Musk cannot expect the market to deliver success simply because he has arrived. docs.title: Kotak Neo's Shrikant Chouhan bullish on BEL, Greenply; check targets
docs.text:
Kotak Neo's Shrikant Chouhan bullish on BEL, Greenply; check targets
 Stocks to buy today: Kotak Neo's Shrikant Chouhan has shared a bullish view on Bharat Electronics Limited and Greenply Industries Limited.
 Kotak Neo's Shrikant Chouhan bullish on BEL, Greenply; check targets
 Shrikant Chouhan Mumbai 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 13 2026 | 7:38 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion. 
 Stocks to buy recommendations by Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research, Kotak Neo 
 Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL): Add 
 CMP: ₹374 
 FV: ₹410 
 RBI steps may steady rupee, but new lows seen by FY27-end: BS Poll premium 
 RBI measures to support rupee weigh on govt bonds, domestic equities
 Defence startup Tonbo Imaging fixes IPO price band at ₹665-700 a share
 Stock Market Close: Sensex sheds 548 pts, Nifty ends at 22,363; FMCG, PSU Bank indices underperform
 Oil prices, yields among key factors behind Sensex's 800 pts intraday fall
 Resistance: ₹383, ₹390 
 Support: ₹366, ₹360 
 Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL) is well positioned to sustain its growth momentum, supported by a strong pipeline of large defence programs, including QRSAM, AMCA and key naval projects such as P75I and NGC. Management expects the year-end order book to exceed Rs1 lakh cr, compared with approximately ₹75,000 crore, which remained broadly flat over the past three years. The anticipated increase will be driven by a healthy pipeline of base orders exceeding ₹25,000 crore and the ₹30,000 crore QRSAM program, significantly strengthening revenue visibility.
 Missiles are emerging as BEL’s second-largest growth vertical after electronics, supported by its participation in key programs such as QRSAM, Pralay, Nirbhay/LRLACM and Project Kusha. Missile revenues are expected to scale up to a high-double-digit share of overall revenues over the next 2–3 years. The approximately ₹30,000 crore QRSAM program remains the most important near-term growth catalyst. Under Project Kusha, India’s indigenous long-range air-defence initiative, BEL is keen to be selected by DRDO as the lead integrator, with BDL manufacturing the missiles.
 In the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) program, BEL is among the three shortlisted consortia following technical evaluation. The company remains hopeful of emerging as the L1 bidder alongside L&T, with an equal work-share arrangement already locked in, offering potential long-term growth opportunities.
 Operationally, BEL has delivered a strong 17 per cent revenue CAGR over FY24–FY26 and continues to guide for revenue growth of over 15 per cent in the medium term. Ebitda margins have expanded to nearly 30 per cent, supported by higher indigenization, operating leverage and a favourable product mix. The expected improvement in order inflows should provide strong revenue visibility over the next 3–4 years.
 Healthy order prospects, improving business mix and sustained visibility on India’s defence spending underpin our constructive outlook on BEL. We maintain our Add rating with a fair value of ₹410, based on an unchanged valuation multiple of 33x September 2028E earnings. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE 
 Greenply Industries Limited (Greenply): Buy 
 CMP: ₹314 
 FV: ₹354 
 Resistance: ₹325, ₹335 
 Support: ₹305, ₹295 
 Greenply Industries Limited (Greenply) business segments include wood based products including plywood and MDF (medium density fiberboard). In the plywood segment, the management has guided 10 per cent volume growth in FY27E. In Q1FY27, plywood volume grew by 13.8 per cent Y-o-Y. Greenply’s plywood volume growth is expected to benefit from BIS implementation, lower imports, investment in ECOTEC brand and internal process improvement. For plywood margins, the management is positive that operating leverage benefits will come into play with higher revenue. We believe that the plywood segment Ebitda margins have scope for improvement, led by operational efficiency and process improvement at its plant. MDF segment is expected to support revenue growth as the company expanded capacity in FY26 and another line is being added. The management has guided 25-30 per cent MDF volume growth in FY27E. MDF volumes grew by 24.7 per cent Y-o-Y in Q1FY27. The company is focusing on selling value added products and that along with improved efficiencies and operating leverage from high volumes is expected to support Ebitda margin in the MDF segment. Further, any correction in timber prices would be an added advantage. The company has taken price hikes in both the timber and the MDF segment in Q1FY27, to pass on the increase in chemical prices and higher logistics cost (in imports). In the plywood segment, the company is constructing a new plant in Odisha with an outlay of ₹130 crore and expanding MDF capacity, that entails an investment of ₹425 crore. We expect the earnings growth momentum to continue in FY27E and FY28E. We have a Buy rating and a fair value of ₹354 on the stock.

docs.title: Buy Campus Activewear; target of Rs 290: Motilal Oswal
docs.text:
Buy Campus Activewear; target of Rs 290: Motilal Oswal
 CAMPUS 
 Motilal Oswal's research report on Campus Activewear 
 We attended Campus Activewear (Campus) analyst meet and came away constructive on management’s mid-teens organic growth ambition, underpinned by volume, premiumization, and expansion into newer categories such as performance footwear. Notably, management indicated its openness to inorganic opportunities (brand licensing/M&A) to strengthen its premium portfolio, marking an additional growth lever, although any such transaction would need to be ASP and margin accretive. Further, Campus remains confident of sustaining its YoY margin expansion, aided by an improving product mix and calibrated price hikes. which it does not intend to roll back even if RM prices moderate. We expect ~15%/18%/23% revenue/ EBITDA/PAT CAGR over FY26-29E, driven by equal contributions from volume and ASP growth. 
 Outlook 
 Our estimates do not factor in any inorganic expansion. After the recent sharp correction, the risk-reward appears compelling. We reiterate our BUY rating on Campus with a TP of INR290, premised on 35x Sep’28 EPS.  AI Summary
 Motilal Oswal has reiterated a buy rating on VA Tech Wabag with a target price of 2,529 per share, citing a strong order book of 20,000 crore, robust bid pipeline, and steady international project execution, indicating an upside potential of up to 30%.
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source 
 Shares of VA Tech Wabag Ltd. have an upside potential of up to 30%, as per brokerage firm Motilal Oswal's latest note on Monday, October 12.
The brokerage has reiterated its "buy" recommendation with a target price of ₹2,529 per share on the stock.
Motilal Oswal said the company remains well-positioned for sustained growth, aided by regular order flows and normal project execution, including in the war-affected West Asia region.
VA Tech Wabag's current order book is worth ₹20,000 crore, which is five times its FY26 revenue. This, and a strong bid pipeline, provides visibility towards 20% revenue growth over the next three to four years, the brokerage said.
It added that VA Tech Wabag's focus remains on profitable growth and the overseas market.
After delivering a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 7% revenue, 17% EBITDA and 28% adjusted profit after tax (APAT) over FY21-26, Motilal Oswal expects these same metrics to grow at a CAGR of 19% 26% and 23% over FY26-28, respectively.
The note further said that strong free cash flow generation, net cash position of ₹1,000 crore and improving return ratios make the stock attractive at 21 times its estimated FY28 price-to-earnings ratio.
 Motilal Oswal said over the past six months, VA Tech Wabag has secured several high-quality orders across a wide range of applications in India and the overseas market.
It recently won a repeat order worth ₹250 crore from Reliance Industries in Jamnagar for EPT work, and entered the Kuwait and UAE markets by bagging orders worth ₹100 crore and ₹600 crore each in the region.
In India, VA Tech Wabag strengthened its long-standing relationships with BWSSB and DJB via new order wins, while in Europe it secured a project in Austria from Donauinsel Water Works, Motilal Oswal said, adding that the Chennai desalination project is steadily moving towards competition as well.
It said overseas projects contribute 50% of the company's revenue and higher share of the order book. Given the critical and non-discretionary nature of desalination plants, its business continuity is expected to remain intact, the brokerage said. 
 The West Asia region and other overseas projects are better placed in terms of working capital cycles and cash flow generation compared to Indian projects, it said.
VA Tech Wabag's intensified focus on executing large-scale projects in high margin segments such as EP, industrial and operational and maintenance augurs well for margins, Motilal Oswal added.
All 13 analysts who have coverage on VA Tech Wabag have "buy" recommendations on it.
Shares of VA Tech Wabag, having gained as much as 6% in early trading on Thursday to ₹2,007.5, have come off the highs of the day and it now trades 1.2% higher at ₹1,960. The stock is up 50% so far this year, but it still 15% away from its record high of ₹2,319, which it had surged to on September 15 this year.

 At the end of the June quarter, Suzlon Energy's order book stood at 5.9 GW, providing 100% visibility on Motilal Oswal's delivery estimates until the third quarter of financial year 2028.
The brokerage expects Suzlon Energy's EBITDA to grow at a Compounded Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 22% over financial year 2026-2028. 
 India added 3 GW of wind capacity in the first half of the current financial year, according to Motilal Oswal, who also said that historically, as the second half installations have been 1.5x of those in H1, the implies addition of nearly 4.5 GW in the second half would take the FY27 additions to nearly 7.5 GW, which is in-line with the Ministry of New & Renewable Energy's expectation of 7.5 GW to 8 GW. 
 Rising power demand, mainly during evening peak hours, should support greater deployment of wind capacity through wind-solar hybrid and FDRE projects, Motilal Oswal said.

 Motilal Oswal wrote in its note that Suzlon's DevCo model has gained strong traction with orders worth over 600 MW booked within four months of the financial year and accounts for 60% of the total orders.
Internationally, Suzlon is also evaluating export opportunities in Europe, Australia, Latin America and Southeast Asia, with Australia and Europe emerging as promising markets, the brokerage noted.
Additionally, repowering in India presents a potential opportunity of up to 25 GW, given that a major portion of the existing wind fleet was commissioned between 10-20 years prior and Suzlon is expecting to secure confirmed repowering orders by the end of the current financial year, with opportunities scaling up in the next two to three years.
Suzlon Energy stands to benefit from regulatory tailwinds mandating local content, a robust providing strong revenue visibility and execution improvements through proactive land acquisitions and EPC expansion initiatives, Motilal Oswal wrote.
12 analysts have coverage on Suzlon Energy, of which 10 have a "buy" rating, and two others have a "hold". No analyst tracking the stock has a "sell" recommendation. The consensus estimates of price targets implies an upside potential of 67% from current levels.

On Monday, the market opened flat near 22,600 but declined towards 22,350 following profit booking.
Chouhan identified 22,300 as a key support level for the Nifty. He said a break below this level could push the index towards 22,150, a level it tested last week. A further decline could trigger stronger selling pressure across the market, he added.
Persistent Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) outflows continue to weigh on market sentiment. Currency depreciation concerns and crude oil prices remaining above USD 100 are adding to investor worries over inflation. 
 Advertisement 
Advising investors on the current market conditions, Chouhan recommended buying fundamentally strong companies at key support levels in phases rather than investing the entire amount at once. He also said the ongoing sideways movement presents an opportunity for Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) investors.
On sectoral opportunities, Chouhan identified defence, automobiles, internet-based businesses and software companies, including new-age technology firms, as key sectors to watch.
He noted that profit booking has affected defensive sectors such as pharmaceuticals ahead of the upcoming second-quarter earnings announcements.
Chouhan said market valuations and earnings indicate attractive levels for investors with a medium- to long-term investment horizon. He advised investors to focus on company fundamentals while making investment decisions. (ANI)
